html:
On 12 September 1683 a relief army led by King John III Sobieski of Poland defeated the Ottoman army besieging Vienna. It marked the end of Ottoman expansion into central Europe.

The grand vizier Kara Mustafa had besieged the city since July with a huge army. The emperor Leopold I had fled, and the defenders were close to collapse when German and Polish troops came down from the Kahlenberg hill. The charge of the Polish winged hussars, the largest cavalry charge in history by some counts, broke the Ottoman camp.

Kara Mustafa was executed on the sultan's orders. In the war that followed, the Habsburgs conquered Hungary, confirmed by the Treaty of Karlowitz in 1699. The Ottoman Empire never again threatened Vienna, as it had in the first siege of 1529. See Austria.
sum: On 12 September 1683 a relief army led by King John III Sobieski of Poland defeated the Ottoman army besieging Vienna. It marked the end of Ottoman expansion into central Europe.
